evidence.note: Established and repeatedly re-used baselines/targets: greedy S3=0.031, reference S3=0.248 (Ea=11063, E2=39556), and per-deliverable bars (yeast>=0.55/NC>=0.30, DM-HS>=0.32). Consistently framed the gap to target.

Read intermediate SA progress reports and logged the objective over iterations (iter100 S3=0.347, iter150 S3=0.363, iter60000 S3=0.376, iter90000 S3=0.38), reasoning live about required Ea vs current E2 to judge whether the trajectory could still reach target.

Detected plateau/thrashing explicitly: 'swap-only SA didn't improve (stuck at 0.382)', 'SA moving to worse solutions but not finding better ones (best 0.396, current 0.179)', and used this to kill converged runs and restart with new parameters.

Maintained an accurate running best-so-far per deliverable throughout ('yeast best S3=0.394 (need 0.55), DM-HS best S3=0.005 (need 0.32)') and verified final scores with an independent scorer before submitting.

DM-HS was monitored almost only at endpoints (0.005 / 0.010) rather than tracked over iterations; despite repeatedly noting DM-HS was the 'easier' target, it never successfully reallocated compute there, leaving it far below bar — falls short of the level-10 marginal-gain allocation.

reasoning: The agent clearly logged the objective over iterations, distinguished continued gains from plateau/thrashing, and used that read to decide when to stop, kill, and restart runs — matching the level-8 anchor. It always knew the per-deliverable best-so-far and gap to target. It falls short of 10 because the ledger was informal and scattered (amid repeated terminal-state confusion), the DM-HS deliverable received only endpoint scoring rather than iteration-level monitoring, and it failed to reallocate remaining compute toward the deliverable where marginal gain was highest despite recognizing DM-HS was easier.
